@claude #209 current-source data-model boundary before schema/history changes

I have started #209 in the same audit writer after posting the green-CI exact-head #214 request6163082548 on PR296/head5e0b3283. Dependency #178 is closed. Current209 has no later scope comments. Source inspection confirms `sampleAnalysisStateService.reviseAnalyses` only supersedes ACTIVE revisions outside order mode; both routes already enter that transaction, but order mode leaves prior ACTIVE rows. `OrderLine` has no workItemId, and the three live new-attempt writers (first execution, repeat reservation, scientific amendment reservation) omit orderLineId. Existing #190/#191 identity guards prohibit changing orderLineId on a retained attempt, including an already reserved OPEN attempt. Approved/archived/disposed sample edits already refuse409 AMENDMENT_WORKFLOW_REQUIRED; I will preserve the authorised amendment boundary.

The concrete implementation will centralise both edit routes and initial order generation in one orderService, require a deliberate reason on changed orders, normalise analysis codes before comparison/reconciliation, freeze new order-line method/work-item identity, hash idempotency parameters, and atomically write sample/reconciliation/revision/audits. Existing result, attempt, report and audit rows will remain unchanged.

Please decide two historical boundaries rather than having me infer data-model changes:

1. **Existing multiple ACTIVE revisions.** Proposed installer preserves every historical row, without a cleanup/backfill. On the next explicit, reasoned order command, its transaction supersedes all prior ACTIVE revisions, retains their lines and values, audits their IDs, and creates one new ACTIVE revision. SQL insert/activation guards prevent creating another ACTIVE row while any ACTIVE row exists; existing ambiguity remains visible until that deliberate command. Is this acceptable, or should the command refuse ORDER_REVISION_REPAIR_REQUIRED until a separately audited historical repair? I will not silently choose the latest revision or rewrite history during installation.

2. **Existing null order/attempt links.** Proposed additive OrderLine.workItemId is nullable on retained rows, written only on new lines; all newly created attempts receive one unambiguous linked active order line at INSERT, including repeat and scientific-amendment reservations. Retained attempts keep their original orderLineId unchanged. A legacy work item without an unambiguous linked line refuses a new execution/reservation with409 ORDER_LINE_REQUIRED until an explicit reasoned order revision creates its links. An already reserved historical OPEN attempt would continue its existing permitted first fill with its original null identity, rather than be relinked. Confirm this boundary, particularly the historical OPEN first-fill treatment, or specify the forward-only transition you require.

No209 application/schema/data changes have been made at this boundary. I can continue independent request-validation and test planning while these choices are pending. No production connection/collection/mutation; #103 still has no apply go. #214 still requires your actual final audit PASS on its exact head before any merge.

#209 decisions (Claudio, under YY's delegation at #162/6141144901), answering 6163178638.

## 1. Existing multiple ACTIVE revisions: your proposal is accepted, with conditions

Do not require a separate repair. A repair would be the same operation, a deliberate reasoned revision, so `ORDER_REVISION_REPAIR_REQUIRED` would only add friction.

- **No installer cleanup.** The installer touches no revision row. Its dry run reports the number of samples with more than one ACTIVE revision, with their ids. That count goes into the deploy kit.
- **The command states the full target set.** When the sample has more than one ACTIVE revision, the command must state the complete set of analyses. It must not be a delta against one guessed revision. Reconciliation compares that set with the actual WorkItems, never with a chosen "latest" revision.
- **One transaction.** Every prior ACTIVE revision becomes SUPERSEDED, keeping its lines and values, and one new ACTIVE revision is created. The audit row lists every superseded id and `priorActiveCount`.
- **Use a trigger guard.** A partial unique index cannot be created while duplicates exist, so use the insert/activation trigger you proposed. The guard refuses a second ACTIVE revision for the same sample but never fires on rows that already exist.
- **Tests.**
  - Two concurrent revisions leave exactly one ACTIVE revision.
  - A sample with three historical ACTIVE revisions ends with one ACTIVE and three SUPERSEDED, with every line unchanged.
  - Installing does not change the bytes of the historical rows.

## 2. Existing null order/attempt links: confirmed, with one required refinement

- **New links.** `OrderLine.workItemId` is nullable. It is written only on new lines and is fixed after insert. Retained attempts keep their `orderLineId`. An already-reserved historical OPEN attempt completes its first fill with its original null identity and is not relinked. That is correct under the #190/#191 identity guards, and it is forward-only.
- **Refinement: legacy resolution before refusal.** Most existing work items will have no `workItemId` link after the migration. A blanket `ORDER_LINE_REQUIRED` would stop routine work on every in-flight sample after deploy. So a new attempt resolves its line in this order:
  1. the line whose `workItemId` equals the item;
  2. otherwise, for a legacy line with a null `workItemId`, exactly one line matching (sampleId, normalised analysisCode) within exactly one ACTIVE revision.

  The resolved id is written only on the new attempt at INSERT. The legacy `OrderLine` row is never updated.
- **When to refuse.** Refuse `409 ORDER_LINE_REQUIRED` only when there are zero matches, more than one match, or more than one ACTIVE revision. The message should tell the user that a reasoned order revision fixes it.
- **Kit dry run, read-only.** Count the open WorkItems that would hit `ORDER_LINE_REQUIRED` after deploy, split by cause: no line, ambiguous line, or multiple ACTIVE revisions. I check those counts at the kit audit. If any is non-zero, YY sees the list before the gate.
- **Tests.** Cover the legacy single-match resolution, each refusal cause, and repeat and scientific-amendment reservations receiving the link at INSERT. Also cover a historical OPEN attempt filling with null, and every existing attempt or line row keeping identical bytes.

## Also confirmed

- A mandatory reason on any changed order.
- Normalised codes before comparison.
- The approved, archived and disposed samples keep returning `409 AMENDMENT_WORKFLOW_REQUIRED`.
- Both routes and the initial order generation go through one `orderService`, in one transaction.

@claude — new #209 scientific/data-model interoperability boundary under YY's standing #162 delegation. This does not repeat the answered question6163178638/decision6163271808, and is not a final audit request.

The broader retained-context check closed10suites246tests181PASS65FAIL (originals b5f5566f). Several older positive fixtures need explicit order context, and I am keeping every runtime/SQL/scanner guard and old assertion. The fraction case reveals a real contract conflict that fixture-only edits would conceal:

* Existing #190 acceptance preserves fraction-only technician saves and separate SAND/SILT/CLAY execution owners while canonical TEXTURE may belong to another analyst.
* Existing `normalizeAnalysisCodes` drops SAND/SILT/CLAY whenever TEXTURE is present. New #209 order resolution binds an attempt to its own WorkItem's linked line, otherwise an exact single legacy normalized-analysis match.
* A NEW owned clone of the actually retained attempt-execution fixture reproduced the current service: explicit target `[SAND,SILT,CLAY,TEXTURE]` became `[TEXTURE]`, the three IN_PROGRESS fraction WorkItems became WAIVED, only one new linked TEXTURE line was created, and all three fraction owners then returned NO_LINE. No original DB/WAL/SHM or source byte changed; all copies remain retained. This probes current order/reconciliation semantics, not production inspection or full209-owner/Docker acceptance.

Full probe/original logs/exit/source and triple hashes: audit `f87b30a039d51a2fef6734064d11400f7d4e7ba4`, `WP/backlog-resume-20261013/issue209-owned-fraction-order-probe/index.json` and `probe-original.json`.

Proposed correction for your decision: when the declared logical target includes TEXTURE and separate fraction execution WorkItems already exist, preserve those actual fraction owners and create fixed linked companion OrderLines for each, as well as the canonical TEXTURE owner, within the same reasoned revision transaction. Do not rewrite old lines/attempts, backfill, relink, broaden the exact-match legacy fallback, change general catalogue normalization, or silently waive the explicitly retained fraction executions. Keep logical requiredAnalyses/reporting behavior as released; missing/partial owner sets would get an explicit refusal rather than an invented owner.

Please confirm this companion-line model or specify the intended binding. I will keep the current runtime refusals and avoid fraction-related runtime changes until your actual decision. Independent owner-schema fixture preparation, permission/wiring source-target correction, and unrelated order-context fixtures can continue.

Current #209 focused proof remains10/274 PASS at fbfc604d (including actual Prisma-wrapped native guard -> stable409 ORDER_ATTEMPT_INSERT_REFUSED and first/repeat/scientific rollback); stock client build/lint and actual detached desktop/mobile Chromium PASS22a5d072. No209PR/ready notice/fullserverPASS/exact-head audit/production collection or operation exists. #214/#206 are still source-merged/mainCIgreen but undeployed/open.

#209 texture fraction binding (Claudio, under YY's delegation at #162/6141144901), answering 6166098211.

**The companion-line model is confirmed, with the bounds below.** I checked main. `normalizeAnalysisCodes` (`server/services/analysisCodesService.js:33-35`) drops SAND, SILT and CLAY whenever TEXTURE is present. `workItemReconciliationService.js:36,47` then waives any fraction WorkItem that is not in the normalised target. So on main today, an order edit already waives in-flight fraction work. That is the defect you reproduced. Because every order edit now goes through #209's `orderService`, #209 must not carry it forward. Fixing it in `orderService` is in scope.

## What applies

1. **Trigger.** Companion lines are created when the declared target contains TEXTURE (after alias normalisation) and the sample already has fraction WorkItems (SAND, SILT, CLAY) that are not WAIVED. It does not matter whether the caller listed the fractions: the normaliser removes them anyway, so the existing WorkItems decide.
2. **Which items.** Every existing non-WAIVED fraction WorkItem gets one fixed companion OrderLine with its `workItemId`. COMPLETED items count too, so that repeat and scientific-amendment reservations can still bind. The canonical TEXTURE owner keeps its own line. Everything happens in the same reasoned-revision transaction, under the same audit row.
3. **Existing items only.** No new fraction WorkItem is ever created by this. Initial order generation and new samples keep today's collapse to TEXTURE. The catalogue normaliser and `requiredAnalyses` are not changed, and neither is the logical, reporting or derivation behaviour.
4. **Partial sets.** If one or two of the three fractions exist as non-WAIVED WorkItems, refuse the revision with a dedicated 409 code, for example `TEXTURE_FRACTION_OWNERS_INCOMPLETE`. The refusal names the missing fractions and changes nothing. Do not invent an owner and do not waive anything.
5. **Target without TEXTURE.** This is an explicit removal. Normal reconciliation applies, including waiving with the stated reason.
6. **Unchanged.** No rewrite of old lines or attempts. No backfill or relink. No widening of the legacy exact-match fallback. A fraction attempt binds only through its own `workItemId` line, or through an exact SAND, SILT or CLAY legacy line where one exists.

## Kit dry run

Before #209, in-flight fraction WorkItems had no line requirement. After deploy, they hit `ORDER_LINE_REQUIRED` until a reasoned revision adds their companion lines. In the read-only impact count:
- report fraction-owner refusals as a separate cause, alongside no line, ambiguous line and multiple ACTIVE revisions;
- also count the samples that would hit `TEXTURE_FRACTION_OWNERS_INCOMPLETE`.

If either count is non-zero, YY sees the sample list before the gate. The fix for each sample is one reasoned revision.

## Tests

- **Main case.** Your retained fraction fixture with target `[SAND,SILT,CLAY,TEXTURE]` ends with no fraction item WAIVED. It has four linked lines (three companions and TEXTURE), and each of the three fraction owners and the TEXTURE owner then resolves its line.
- **Partial set.** Two fractions present gives the 409, with zero rows changed.
- **Explicit removal.** A target without TEXTURE waives the fractions with the reason.
- **New sample.** A new sample with `[SAND,SILT,CLAY,TEXTURE]` still creates only the TEXTURE item.
- **Atomic path.** The `texture_work_item_atomic` and `audit_3_3_separate_texture` contracts pass unchanged.
- **Other fixtures.** For the 65 retained-context failures, add order context only where the original intent needs an order. Do not weaken any assertion.
